To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the circadian rhythm of hepatic G6Phosphatase and InPPhasphatase activity is expressed with a high amplitude and with a phase difference of 5.34 hr among them.
G6Pase activity is regulated by a circadian rhythm in the liver and the rhythm is in phase with InPPase activity.
the activities of G6P, InP and ATP in liver tissue of male Swiss albino mice exhibit circadian rhythmicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the circadian rhythmicity of hepatic phosphatases in mouse liver and their interrelationships.
circadian rhythm in a group of phosphatases in mouse liver and their possible physiological significance.
the circadian rhythmometric analysis and phase shift of G6Pases and other hepatic phosphohydrolytic enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
G6Pase activity is under a circadian regulation and the rhythmicity of the activity is not a consequence of the rhythmicity in InPPase activity.
G6Pase activity is rhythmic and oscillates in a circadian fashion with a high amplitude and with a phase lag of 5.34 hr in relation to InPPase.
G6Pase oscillates in phase with InPPase and AlPase and ATPase with an amplitude of about 0.5 and 1.2 respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
circadian rhythm in hepatic phosphohydrolytic activities is not only a function of the time scale of measurement but also depends on the enzyme substrate used.
G6Pase activity is regulated by a circadian clock, whereas InPPase is regulated both by the clock and by the substrate.

G6Pase oscillates across the mean value of 0.4 U with an amplitude 0.44 and acrophase at 194.3 degrees (13.4 hr) whereas InPPase oscillates across mean value 2.8 U with amplitude 1.15 and acrophase 114.1 (8.0).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the circadian rhythms of G6P, InPP and AlPase in mouse liver are not related to each other.
the circadian rhythm in hepatic enzymes is not only a function of the tissue, but is a complex function of the enzyme itself.

circadian rhythms are not restricted to a single enzyme or metabolic process but are a property of the whole organism and are a manifestation of the integrated activity of a large number of biochemical and physiological processes.
